Direct shear test on RC2 soil (Red Crushed Volcanic Scoria (Broadly graded)), loose; apparatus: direct shear (University of Notre Dame). Recorded: peak shear strength vs normal stress with least-squares line (Univac 1107, CAL-COMP plot).

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The numbers below were digitized from the published figure by two readings made separately; they agree within the stated reading bounds at 18 of the 20 points, and the rest were settled against the scan. Student reviewers have looked at 12 of the 20 points on the scan; two reviewers confirmed all of them (see the provenance page). The test setup is incomplete: relative density Dr, specimen height, normal stress, held constant, displacement rate are not reported.
:::

## Data

![shear strength (peak shear stress) against normal stress, SI units. Error bars are reading bounds (half-widths from the digitization), not standard deviations. Filled markers were agreed by both readings, hollow ones were not.](../img/plots/b68-ds-fc-12.png){.lightbox}

Peak shear strength (peak shear stress) 207.3 kPa at 215.5 kPa normal stress; 215.9 kPa at 224.2 kPa, the end of the record.

Download: [observations.csv](../files/data/experiments/b68-ds-fc-12/observations.csv) (20 points: 8 plotted symbols, 9 samples of the drawn curve; columns `x_si`, `y_si` with bounds `x_bound_si`, `y_bound_si`; panel 1: shear strength (peak shear stress) in Pa against normal stress in Pa; the printed-unit values, the pixel position on the scan and the review status of each point are kept in further columns) and [series.json](../files/data/experiments/b68-ds-fc-12/series.json) (units, conversion factors, how the points were read).

Reading bounds on this figure (how far our reading of the printed figure may be off, not the uncertainty of the test): typical bound 858 Pa in normal stress, 1.0 kPa in shear strength (0.5 percent of the peak). Both independent readings agree within these bounds at 18 of the 20 points; the other 2 were settled against the scan (read by one reader and verified by the other, or decided between two readings). [Check the digitized points against the scan](../figures/index.qmd#check-fc-12).
